scope: Movement C1/C2 and Active Living B1/B2 source-fit proposals: 109 records. Safety B3, Healthy Living and integrated A1 remain pending qualification.
meaning: Original untested task design, not a child-performance study, clinical prescription, fitness ranking or learner-state update.

protocols.task: On a clear floor route, choose stable shapes on different appropriate bases and at low/middle/higher accessible levels. Perform two still positions and a controlled transfer between them, then vary speed or route and recover a deliberately small self-initiated change. Repeat with an appropriate lightweight object and in relation to a partner: coordinate side-by-side shapes or mirror a change without unsafe supporting/lifting. Older source rows retain smooth transfers in relation to another person and equipment; a single held pose is insufficient.
protocols.positive: The learner maintains or recovers intended body control and shows a useful adjustment, not only labels balance.
protocols.nearMiss: One frozen position, unsafe partner loading or an adult holding the learner in place does not establish the whole operation.
protocols.transfer: Change the base, safe route or partner position and demonstrate a controlled adjustment.
protocols.sourceConditions: Preserve each exact source row’s body/shape/level, equipment, partner and transfer duties. The unrelated NCERT60-second posture is not imported as an Ontario norm.

protocols.task: Use a marked clear route to walk/run, hop, skip, jump and land, then respond to direction, stop and speed cues. Combine patterns at different levels and pathways with/without a lightweight object and with a partner at a safe distance. Grade1 separately demonstrates stopping near people/equipment. Grade2 includes actual one- and two-foot take-offs; Grade3 chooses height or distance and demonstrates both take-off types. Grade4 includes an actual appropriately low supported take-off height and controlled landing with a prepared adult/surface; no fixed bench height or distance score. Grade5 changes body actions for a controlled height/distance jump. Grade6 combines varied routes, speeds and others/equipment.
protocols.positive: Recognisably different movement patterns remain controlled through the source-specific combination or landing condition.
protocols.nearMiss: Naming movements, one successful unplanned jump or merely walking the route cannot certify the whole canonical pattern inventory.
protocols.transfer: Change the path/cue order or object arrangement and retain control.
protocols.sourceConditions: Actual safe capability/access and adult-prepared environment retained; wheelchair/adapted source participation is not falsely recorded as mastery of every canonical walk/run/hop pattern.

protocols.task: Use a soft ball, beanbag and light disc or similarly appropriate shapes. Deliberately send by hand and foot at changed safe levels/directions/distances, receive a changed incoming path and control arrival. Older rows include an appropriate hand/implement strike and a receiving aid, with actual speed/force adjustment and an explained/demonstrated movement principle such as following the intended direction or absorbing arrival. Keep a foot-stop/other body receiving case as an explicit source task where required; a hand catch alone never proves that case.
protocols.positive: Intentional release/contact, safe body positioning and adjusted controlled arrival are actually demonstrated across the selected source variety.
protocols.nearMiss: Accidental contact, one unadjusted throw or only identifying an equipment picture is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Move the target/partner or change the supplied object’s path, speed or equipment and adapt.
protocols.sourceConditions: No universal distance, dominance or athletic norm. The whole existing hand-catching and throwing checks remain separate from a source-specific foot/equipment condition.

protocols.task: Secure a suitable object, then retain control while moving through a clear changing route. Use more than one object size/shape and holding arrangement: hands, forearm/body support and an appropriate scoop or similar aid. Change speed, path and relation to another person/obstacle. For Grade6 use a no-contact modified keep-away or route-change situation with clear boundaries, maintaining possession while choosing a new path. Controlled carrying is a valid source implementation; continuous dribbling is an illustrative option, not an invented universal duty. If selected, actual foot/stick dribbling must be demonstrated rather than inferred from hand catching.
protocols.positive: The object remains deliberately controlled through the required movement changes, not merely caught once at the beginning.
protocols.nearMiss: An isolated catch, walking without the object, repeatedly dropping it or a static posed photo is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Change object, support/aid, route and other-person position and adapt the retention.
protocols.sourceConditions: Whole Catching includes secure retention during modest travel; combine with actual locomotor control and the precise source conditions, without silently redefining either old claim.

protocols.task: Actually play more than one individual and small-group activity from the original game set. Identify its goal, space/boundaries, allowed movement/equipment, relevant roles and agreed safety/fair-play rules. Explain two rules and what would happen without them, then apply them consistently. Share an idea, respond to another participant and complete an agreed fair role. Take turns and listen; an adult’s repeated reminders or the group result alone do not prove an individual whole claim.
protocols.positive: The learner connects an actual game component to how the activity works and participates accordingly.
protocols.nearMiss: Reciting a rule word or describing only the equipment without applying the activity’s components is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Play a changed version with a different boundary, role or allowed action and explain/apply the new structure.
protocols.sourceConditions: No winner/fitness/positive mood criterion. Group-work, rules vocabulary and their actual hard-chain checks remain; the source is not reduced to an English word quiz.

protocols.task: After actually playing examples from different activity families, sort the original activity cards by the supplied functional model: accuracy at a target; return across a divided area; striking then retrieving to limit runs; retaining/advancing possession against opposition; individual non-opposition task. Explain a common feature and an effective observed tactic for the chosen families. Count the cards in each group, compare totals and order the categories by count to retain the complete existing classification/count operation; that extra whole-card check is not a new HPE numeric requirement.
protocols.positive: Classification follows the actual rules/objective/interaction, not colour of equipment or country/name; reasoning is tied to actual participation.
protocols.nearMiss: Only naming five labels, sorting by ball colour or claiming that all activities use one universal taxonomy is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Classify a changed original game from its declared rules and justify it; a game may require stating the chosen dominant structure when features overlap.
protocols.sourceConditions: The official source calls its chart one possible model. No new five-category mastery topic or compulsory team-sport preference.

protocols.task: In an actual modified game, pause or use an agreed decision break to identify two plausible actions and a likely consequence of each under the current objective, rules, space and other-player positions. Choose with a reason, perform the action, inspect the result and make a fresh decision when the situation changes. For younger rows use changed target distance or a clear versus blocked route. Older rows use an unmarked receiver, placing a return away from an opponent, positioning to retrieve, or protecting possession without contact. Do not interpret “stop” as a demand to freeze bodily movement before every live action.
protocols.positive: A reasoned choice is physically applied and adapted to a changed game situation; fluent motor execution alone does not prove the decision criterion.
protocols.nearMiss: An accurate pass to a covered option, a memorised tactic name, a discussion without action or a lucky point alone is insufficient.
protocols.transfer: Change the target, defender position or activity family, identify the new options/consequences and actually apply a suitable choice.
protocols.sourceConditions: Whole Stop, Think, Then Choose is domain-general and its consequence prerequisite remains. No sport-specific decision clone, automatic design/study-strategy transfer or new hard dependency is inferred.

protocols.task: Implement a varied rotation of individual and small-group physical activities across days: a comfortable travel/route activity, an object game, a movement-to-music activity and a cooperative task. Record actual participation according to capabilities and the activity-specific access arrangements. Observe knowing the task, readiness, respectful communication, fair contribution and response to others; a passive worksheet is not participation. Use the actual games and movement tasks already specified in the movement programme.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: For group-work contribution retain own idea, response to another idea and completion of a fair part. For rules retain reasons for two relevant agreements, consistent following and a reasoned no-rule contrast. Keep these checks separate from a general impression of compliance or enthusiasm.

protocols.task: After actual participation in several individual and group activities, identify and compare factors affecting the learner’s own experience. Use an activity-choice card and before/after access adjustment: for example a more accessible play area, a manageable group size or a meaningful choice of role. Explain what helped, what did not and a possible change. No requirement to like every activity or to disclose culture, disability, family circumstances or private feelings.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The self-knowledge contribution is about preferences and strengths, not a claim that liking PE establishes all identity knowledge. Retain the broader existing All about me checks with safely chosen important people/helpers and similarities/differences, without forced private disclosure.

protocols.task: Use an actual school-day map and supplied local home/community opportunity cards: a safe walk/wheel route, free movement space, an indoor alternative and a paid/distant option. Identify realistic daily opportunities and reasons. Older panels compare cost, travel, time, access, peer/cultural relevance and preferences, then propose a feasible response to an obstacle rather than blame the child or family. Test a changed case such as a closed outdoor space or unavailable transport.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: For the routine contribution retain a real chosen routine, when/how plan, week record, reflection and one way to support someone else. For a decision contribution compare at least two feasible options and likely consequences before choosing; naming a barrier alone is not a solution.

protocols.task: Provide the source-required daily minimum 20-minute physical-activity opportunity with appropriate gradual warm-up and cool-down, moderate-to-vigorous participation to the best of each learner’s ability and actual access/support. Prepare a safe adult-supervised circuit from movement tasks, movement-to-music, travel and modified games. Record date, actual activity, duration, preparation, recovery and access/support; do not count an invented example log as a learner’s participation. A gentle cool-down is explicitly taught and performed, not inferred from doing the warm-up.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Preserve the complete preparation claim: follow or choose a suitable gradual sequence, controlled comfortable mobility, a relevant preparation reason communicated by demonstration/picture/explanation, and adjustment for discomfort. Leadership, maximal exertion and pain tolerance are not criteria.

protocols.task: Compare safe activity cases and explain practical physical and mental/brain-health benefits using the grade panel: physical examples include sustained activity, muscular work or easier comfortable movement; mental examples include attention and memory support or reduced risk of depression. Use population-level possibilities, not a promise that a session makes every child happy or cures distress. Younger panels use concrete attention, energy and enjoyable social participation cases; do not require diagnosis or detailed organ physiology.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The Basic Body Needs link contributes exercise/heart/muscle and body-needs reasoning. Retain its full food-energy, water-hydration, sleep-rest/growth and exercise checks separately. It does not alone certify the mental-health part; the explicit cases and explanations supply that source duty. Do not add advanced physiology or harmful-substance knowledge as a new prerequisite for explaining an everyday benefit.

concreteCases.reason: Repeated appropriate participation can develop cardiorespiratory capacity and the ability to sustain activity; an immediate faster heartbeat is a response, not itself proof of improvement.

concreteCases.case: Manageable brief and repeated resistance tasks
concreteCases.reason: Relate suitable muscular work to force or continued effort; no maximal load or body-shape inference.
Relate range to easier movement in an activity; do not claim every stretch prevents injury or require a universal range.

concreteCases.case: An accessible familiar activity followed by a learning task
concreteCases.reason: Discuss attention/memory support as a possible benefit supported by child-specific public guidance; do not require that this particular child immediately feels happy or concentrates better.

protocols.task: Use the complete original four-component concept guide and its contrasting everyday cases, overlap/changed-purpose task and unsupported-inference diagnostic. Explain functional capacity and a relevant everyday benefit. This supplies G5 B2.2’s knowledge duty; its G6 links are conceptual components only.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Keep all four components and functional contrasts, strength versus repeated effort, justified overlap, changed-goal transfer and rejection of appearance/single-result inference. No personal performance norm is assessed by the knowledge task.

protocols.task: Use safe prepared actual activity with adult supervision and suitable individual access. Record ordinary responses before, during and after activity: perceived effort, breathing, warmth and, where appropriate and accessible, a gently found wrist pulse. Younger panels identify signs; later panels compare degree using an accessible simple method such as speaking comfort, breath sounds or perceived exertion. Explain relevant personal/context factors with a hypothetical comparison rather than private medical disclosure. Stop or adapt for discomfort; no deliberate heat, poor-air, cold or exhausted trial.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The Heart & Blood component retains the pump, continuous circulation, vessels reaching the body and appropriate heartbeat/pulse explanation. Feeling a pulse alone is not that full claim, and the full anatomy check does not by itself supply judging degree of exertion. Never enact injury/cut prompts. One elevated pulse is not lasting improvement or a diagnosis.

protocols.task: Create an actual repeated-observation portfolio under suitable adult supervision. Grade 5 chooses one component; Grade 6 considers all four. Use manageable comparable activity observations: a comfortable sustained route, brief suitable resistance action, repetition of a manageable action and comfortable joint motion as appropriate. Record the declared task/purpose, date, response and relevant support/context across occasions; compare with the person’s own earlier comparable evidence and state limitations. No maximum load, timed exhaustion, universal range, percentile or comparison of bodies is used.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: The routine contribution retains actual tracking and reflection. The fitness concept supplies distinctions, not the observations. A blank template makes the source-fit assessment design available but does not claim a child has supplied the evidence. Changes in task or support must be acknowledged, not misread as measured adaptation.

protocols.task: Choose a realistic interest-based activity goal with a timeframe, identify steps, act on the plan on actual occasions, record progress and revise a step when necessary. Grade 2 also participates in a group goal with fair contributions; later panels use actual self-assessment and preferences to choose relevant fitness focus. Grade 5 chooses one component; Grade 6 uses assessment across the four-component model in planning. A plan written but never acted on does not fulfil implementation.
protocols.wholeClaimChecks: Retain the full goal-setting operation, including timeframe, steps, monitoring and adjustment. The routine panel includes the week record and a way to support another person; no forced disclosure or invented difficulty/frustration is needed. Hard-path mindset/mistake checks stay distinct rather than inferring a belief from goal completion.

originalGameSet.objective: Send a soft object into a marked target.
originalGameSet.rules: Throw/roll from the chosen line; retrieve only after the area is clear.
originalGameSet.tacticalChange: Compare a nearer/larger target with a farther/smaller one, or adjust direction after a miss.
originalGameSet.variety: Beanbag-to-hoop, soft-ball-to-wide-zone and disc-to-floor-mark supply three card cases.

originalGameSet.objective: Return a soft object over a low divider into the other clear area.
originalGameSet.rules: Use the agreed hand/paddle action and bounce allowance; stay in the own area, no body contact.
originalGameSet.tacticalChange: Choose an open landing area, then move to a ready position when the opponent’s position changes.
originalGameSet.variety: A hand-return version and a safe short-paddle version supply two card cases.

originalGameSet.objective: A sender strikes/kicks an object, then travels between two safe marks while fielders retrieve and secure it at a base.
originalGameSet.rules: Use separate movement lanes and a clear send signal; no hard throws at people or physical tagging.
originalGameSet.tacticalChange: Choose an unoccupied sending area or a useful retrieval/base position and adapt after a change.
originalGameSet.variety: A soft hand-strike and a foot-send version supply two card cases.

originalGameSet.objective: Keep a soft object and advance it to an agreed receiving zone.
originalGameSet.rules: Use a no-contact small-group pass game; intercept only a free ball, never take from a person’s hands.
originalGameSet.tacticalChange: Compare a covered and an open passing route, then change position to support a return pass.

originalGameSet.objective: Complete an own controlled movement/balance route.
originalGameSet.rules: Follow the safe route and cues, adapting to available access; no opponent or speed ranking.
originalGameSet.tacticalChange: Choose a manageable pace or a stable approach before a turn/transition.
originalGameSet.variety: A travelling route and a balance-transition route supply two card cases.

integratedSelPanel.scope: Actual Movement-strand applications; does not prematurely certify all six A1 source duties across the still-pending Active/Healthy Living contexts.
task: Name an actual ordinary feeling or comfort/uncertainty during learning and notice a partner’s expressed cue; no upset is manufactured.
Identify a manageable challenge and an appropriate support/help request; use a different safe approach or stop an uncomfortable action rather than force it.
Choose a practical practice intention and reflect on the approach/effort; optimism, confidence and liking can vary and are not compliance scores.
Share space/equipment, listen and respond to another person, respect a boundary and support fair participation.
Identify an actual body-control strength/next step without comparing bodies or requiring private disclosure.
Consider actual options/consequences and explain a choice in the physical task.
integratedSelPanel.limits: The full integrated A1 review remains pending with B/D; a successful game does not establish all affective or social mastery.

wholeClaimChecks.movement: Keep the whole existing locomotor pattern inventory, still/moving balance and actual sending/receiving adjustment checks; an adapted source route is not automatic evidence for every canonical movement pattern.
wholeClaimChecks.decision: Retain the full options→consequences→reasoned choice operation and its consequence prerequisite. Actual changed-game action is separately required; no new sport-only decision state.
wholeClaimChecks.classification: Use ten original activity cards in counts3/2/2/1/2, identify functional features, count/order category totals. Separately retain complete count-out/arranged/scattered/cardinality/one-to-one checks up to20 where the hard chain is assessed; those are not additional HPE curriculum mandates.
wholeClaimChecks.rulesAndGroup: Explain actual rules and their safe/fair purpose, follow them without repeated prompting, contribute/respond/complete an agreed role, listen and take turns. No individual competence is inferred from the team result, a smile or covert surveillance.
wholeClaimChecks.activeLiving: All about me retains the complete identity/helper/similarity checks without forced disclosure; body-needs retains food, water, sleep and exercise explanations. Heart retains continuous pumping and vessels, not just a pulse reading. Goal-setting retains actual timeframe/steps/monitoring/adjustment; routine retains a week record/reflection/helping another person. These whole checks are distinct from source-specific participation, exertion and longitudinal duties.
wholeClaimChecks.inheritedGoalPath: Existing hard paths through task steps, mindset and learning from mistakes remain unchanged. Keep their full checks separate: completing a goal does not automatically establish a mindset belief, and lack of visible cheerfulness or distress is not a gap criterion. No dependency is weakened to force an HPE link.

conditions.sourceExamples: Official examples and prompts are optional implementations of comparable complexity; the programme does not turn each sport, body part or example into a new topic.
conditions.sourceAge: Source says development is age-related, not age-dependent. Exact grade associations use the existing Ontario primary age windows; they are not a birthday deadline or universal ability/fitness norm.
conditions.actualPerformance: Use actual controlled movement and actual modified-game application. Classification, spoken discussion and adult demonstration do not replace a production duty.
conditions.access: Prepare appropriate clear space, soft/light equipment and adult-supported access. Adapt source participation to the learner’s capabilities; do not equate an accessible alternative with every fixed whole-card motor requirement.
conditions.sourceHierarchy: The six SEL source skills are integrated in content strands. Their complete A1 dispositions are not inferred from this C1/C2 checkpoint.
conditions.retention: Keep actual possession through the route changes. Continuous dribbling is an illustrative option, not an invented universal requirement; if chosen, assess it directly rather than infer it from a catch.
conditions.state: No new claims, dependencies, clinical/fitness scores, learner observations or database changes.
conditions.activeLiving: Daily actual opportunity, personal factors, access, mental/physical benefit explanations, before/during/after exertion and implemented goals remain grade-specific tasks. No positive mood, appearance, fitness norm or numerical superiority is required.
conditions.longitudinalAssessment: Grade 5 assesses a selected component; Grade 6 assesses all four, with actual repeated observations and implemented interest-based plans. Conceptual answers or a prepared blank record do not constitute a child record or successful implementation.
